close_reason: Bitmask design documented with INVARIANT comment in code
description: Tracking which name types have EVER been constrained via a separate bitmask (nc_constrained_types) is the correct solution to the empty-intersection enforcement problem: if CA1 permits 'example.com' DNS names and CA2 permits 'otherdomain.com' DNS names, the intersection is empty, but the type IS constrained — so any DNS SAN must fail. A design that only inspects nc_permitted to determine 'is this type constrained?' would incorrectly admit DNS names when the intersection is empty. The bitmask prevents that. Defend this design against refactoring that derives constrained-ness from nc_permitted contents.
title: nc_constrained_types bitmask design correctly handles empty-intersection case
